name: temp-core-loop-stability
description: Small-signal .ac loop-gain testbench for temp_core's error amplifier loop (issue #274). Breaks the loop at PG -- the amplifier's own output stays on that node (probed via v(xdut.pg)); the two mirror-gate connections that actually close the loop (XMP1, XMP2) move to a new node PG_FB the testbench injects an AC test signal onto. Reports the closed-loop-equivalent open-loop gain T(jw) = V(xdut.pg)/V(pg_fb), its unity-gain crossover frequency, phase margin there, and gain margin at the frequency the loop phase crosses zero. POST-LAYOUT SIBLING (issue #298, closes the one temp_core testbench tracker #145 left without an extracted sibling): identical stimulus and checks to sim/temp-core-loop-stability/testbench/tb.json except that 'netlist' names a hand-forked fragment of layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice instead of design/netlist/temp_core.spice -- the loop-break edits move inside the subcircuit body, which sim/build_tb.py's verbatim-copy mechanism cannot do, so this fragment is hand-maintained rather than a POSTLAYOUT_FRAGMENTS entry, exactly like its schematic sibling is not a FRAGMENTS entry. See testbench-postlayout/tb_temp_core_loop_stability_postlayout.spice's header for the break-point construction against the extracted instance names (X36/X47/X38/X45 -> PG_FB, X40/X43 left on PG) and design/temp_core.md's 'Error amplifier' section for the topology this loop implements.
claim: POST-LAYOUT RE-RUN (issue #298, the gap tracker #145 disclosed) of the schematic-level record 20260819-182610-a4eebe7 in sim/temp-core-loop-stability/records/, same stimulus and same checks, DUT swapped from design/netlist/temp_core.spice to a hand-forked loop-break fragment of layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice. Any check that flips from PASS on that record to FAIL here is a REGRESSION to flag and route to its owning design issue, not to absorb -- the schematic-vs-extracted comparison is generated by sim/postlayout_delta.py into the paired <record-id>-postlayout-delta derived record. The original claim, unchanged, follows. --- design/temp_core.md#loop-stability -- not a spec/target-spec.md claim: issue #274's own scoping question ('does a phase-margin bound belong in spec/target-spec.md?') is resolved here as 'not yet' -- every sim/temp-core-*/ transient record already shows the loop settling cleanly at every PVT point with no ringing or non-convergence, so there is no evidence of an actual instability problem motivating a new ratified bound today. This record closes the coverage gap (a quantified phase/gain margin has never been measured for this loop against the extracted netlist) and gives design/temp_core.md something to cite instead of merely naming the gap; promoting a specific number to spec/target-spec.md is left as a separate, deliberate decision (its own decision record) for whenever a concrete margin requirement is actually needed. Deterministic corners only (design.ngspice sets sw_stat_mismatch=0) -- mismatch on this loop's own devices is out of scope for a stability-margin measurement (mismatch perturbs the DC operating point and the input-referred offset, not the small-signal loop dynamics around it).
netlist_provenance_note: layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice's own header (layout/postlayout/AUDIT.md): 115 drawn devices (27 nfet_03v3, 28 pfet_03v3, 9 pnp_10p00x10p00, 50 ppolyf_u, 1 cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield) with first-order interconnect R/C on 69/73 nets (138 parasitic cards, sigma R = 65734 ohm, sigma C = 1552.3 fF), net names restored through klt lvs's own 73/73 net correspondence. NOT from the layout: 4 body/well/plate nets (NW1 -> VDD, NW2 -> NT, NWQ -> VSS, vsubs -> VSS) tied to the net the SCHEMATIC puts them on -- the extraction deck's connectivity stack does not reach an Nwell, a substrate ring or a bipolar base well, so they extract isolated and would otherwise float. No ideal device: XCC (cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield, 12u x 12u on PG/NZ, DR-028/#259) is DRAWN and routed to its schematic nets -- every golden device in this cell is drawn, so this loop's own compensation pole is a genuine post-layout claim, not a schematic one. Everything -- MOS, vertical PNP, poly resistor bodies and the MiM cap alike -- is a real extraction of drawn geometry; the one MiM cap is emitted as cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield rather than the deck's cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield (klayout-tools#315) -- the drawn geometry is the schematic's either way, only the deck's name differs. The loop-break fragment itself additionally loads node PG with the extracted interconnect RPG/CPG (5100.563 ohm / 61.7 fF) -- the amplifier's own output metal -- while PG_FB, the two feedback-closing mirror gates broken out for AC injection, carries no separate interconnect model in this extraction (see testbench-postlayout/tb_temp_core_loop_stability_postlayout.spice's header).

dc_bias_delta_mv.description: the loop-break injection source (DC value 0) must reproduce the true closed-loop DC operating point exactly -- v(xdut.pg) and v(pg_fb) are the same physical node in layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice, so a 0 V DC source between them is indistinguishable from the wire it replaces. A nonzero delta here means the break technique is loading the circuit (see testbench-postlayout/tb.json's description and sim/temp-core-designer-check's own post-layout vptat/vctat DC records for the closed-loop cross-check this substitutes for).

phase_margin_deg.description: sanity bound only, not a spec target -- see design/temp_core.md's 'Loop stability' note and issue #274's 'What to do': no phase-margin bound is ratified in spec/target-spec.md yet. This just catches a computation error (e.g. a missed unit conversion) producing a value outside what a phase in degrees can ever be.
